blocks.en: 📖 Evangelism — Unit 9: Obstacles to Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Evangelismo — Unidad 9: Obstáculos para el Evangelismo

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary · Dr. Wayne Cook, Author and Professor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Seminary Director
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala · Dr. Wayne Cook, Autor y Profesor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Director del Seminario

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: While the command to evangelize is clear and the message of the gospel is powerful, many believers struggle to carry out this responsibility. The difficulty is not always due to a lack of knowledge, but often due to obstacles that hinder effective witness. Understanding these obstacles is essential. When they are identified and addressed biblically, the believer is freed to engage in evangelism with greater clarity and confidence.
blocks.es_reference: Aunque el mandato de evangelizar es claro y el mensaje del evangelio es poderoso, muchos creyentes luchan por cumplir esta responsabilidad. La dificultad no siempre se debe a la falta de conocimiento, sino a menudo a obstáculos que estorban un testimonio eficaz. Comprender estos obstáculos es esencial. Cuando se identifican y se abordan bíblicamente, el creyente queda libre para participar en el evangelismo con mayor claridad y confianza.

blocks.en: I. Fear of Rejection
blocks.es_reference: I. El Temor al Rechazo

blocks.en: One of the most common obstacles is fear of rejection. The believer may fear being ridiculed, misunderstood, or dismissed. Jesus warned:
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los obstáculos más comunes es el temor al rechazo. El creyente puede temer ser ridiculizado, malentendido o desestimado. Jesús advirtió:

blocks.en: "Remember the word that I said to you, 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you." (John 15:20, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Acordaos de la palabra que yo os he dicho: El siervo no es mayor que su señor. Si a mí me han perseguido, también a vosotros os perseguirán." (Juan 15:20, RVG)

blocks.en: Rejection is not unusual in evangelism. It is to be expected. The message of the gospel confronts sin and challenges the heart, and not all will respond positively. However, the believer must remember that rejection of the message is not necessarily rejection of the messenger. Faithfulness requires speaking truth regardless of response.
blocks.es_reference: El rechazo no es inusual en el evangelismo. Es de esperarse. El mensaje del evangelio confronta el pecado y desafía el corazón, y no todos responderán positivamente. Sin embargo, el creyente debe recordar que el rechazo del mensaje no es necesariamente el rechazo del mensajero. La fidelidad requiere hablar la verdad sin importar la respuesta.

blocks.en: II. Fear of Inadequacy
blocks.es_reference: II. El Temor a la Insuficiencia

blocks.en: Many believers feel unqualified to evangelize. They believe they do not know enough, cannot answer difficult questions, or lack the ability to communicate clearly. Moses expressed a similar concern:
blocks.es_reference: Muchos creyentes se sienten no calificados para evangelizar. Creen que no saben lo suficiente, que no pueden responder preguntas difíciles, o que carecen de la habilidad para comunicarse con claridad. Moisés expresó una preocupación similar:

blocks.en: "O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before nor since You have spoken to Your servant; but I am slow of speech and slow of tongue." (Exodus 4:10, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "¡Ay, Señor! nunca he sido hombre de fácil palabra, ni antes, ni desde que tú hablas a tu siervo; porque soy tardo en el habla y torpe de lengua." (Éxodo 4:10, RVG)

blocks.en: God's response was not to excuse Moses, but to remind him of divine sufficiency. The believer does not need to know everything. He must simply be faithful to communicate what he does know and trust God with the rest.
blocks.es_reference: La respuesta de Dios no fue excusar a Moisés, sino recordarle la suficiencia divina. El creyente no necesita saberlo todo. Simplemente debe ser fiel para comunicar lo que sí sabe y confiar a Dios lo demás.

blocks.en: III. Misplaced Responsibility
blocks.es_reference: III. Responsabilidad Mal Entendida

blocks.en: Another obstacle is a misunderstanding of responsibility. Some believers feel that they must convince the sinner, produce a response, and ensure conversion. This leads to pressure, anxiety, and sometimes manipulation. Scripture teaches:
blocks.es_reference: Otro obstáculo es un malentendido de la responsabilidad. Algunos creyentes sienten que deben convencer al pecador, producir una respuesta y asegurar la conversión. Esto conduce a la presión, la ansiedad y, a veces, la manipulación. Las Escrituras enseñan:

blocks.en: "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase." (1 Corinthians 3:6, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Yo planté, Apolos regó; pero el crecimiento lo ha dado Dios." (1 Corintios 3:6, RVG)

blocks.en: The believer's responsibility is to proclaim the gospel faithfully. The work of conviction and conversion belongs to God.
blocks.es_reference: La responsabilidad del creyente es proclamar el evangelio fielmente. La obra de convicción y conversión pertenece a Dios.

blocks.en: IV. Lack of Urgency
blocks.es_reference: IV. Falta de Urgencia

blocks.en: A subtle but serious obstacle is a lack of urgency. If the believer does not truly grasp the seriousness of sin and the reality of judgment, evangelism becomes optional rather than essential. Jesus spoke of eternal consequences:
blocks.es_reference: Un obstáculo sutil pero serio es la falta de urgencia. Si el creyente no comprende verdaderamente la seriedad del pecado y la realidad del juicio, el evangelismo se vuelve opcional en lugar de esencial. Jesús habló de consecuencias eternas:

blocks.en: "And these will go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into eternal life." (Matthew 25:46, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "E irán éstos al castigo eterno, y los justos a la vida eterna." (Mateo 25:46, RVG)

blocks.en: Evangelism is not merely a helpful activity—it is a necessary response to the condition of lost humanity.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo no es meramente una actividad útil—es una respuesta necesaria a la condición de la humanidad perdida.

blocks.en: V. Distractions and Priorities
blocks.es_reference: V. Distracciones y Prioridades

blocks.en: Modern life presents many distractions: work, entertainment, and competing responsibilities. These can crowd out the priority of evangelism. Jesus warned:
blocks.es_reference: La vida moderna presenta muchas distracciones: el trabajo, el entretenimiento y responsabilidades que compiten. Estas pueden desplazar la prioridad del evangelismo. Jesús advirtió:

blocks.en: "and the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful." (Mark 4:19, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "pero los afanes de este siglo, y el engaño de las riquezas, y las codicias de otras cosas, entrando, ahogan la palabra, y se hace infructuosa." (Marcos 4:19, RVG)

blocks.en: The believer must examine his priorities and ensure that evangelism is not neglected.
blocks.es_reference: El creyente debe examinar sus prioridades y asegurarse de que el evangelismo no sea descuidado.

blocks.en: VI. Misunderstanding the Gospel
blocks.es_reference: VI. Malentendido del Evangelio

blocks.en: If the gospel itself is unclear, evangelism will be ineffective. Some may omit key elements, simplify the message beyond recognition, or distort it. This results in confusion and false assurance. Clarity in the gospel is essential for faithful witness.
blocks.es_reference: Si el evangelio mismo no es claro, el evangelismo será ineficaz. Algunos pueden omitir elementos clave, simplificar el mensaje más allá de lo reconocible, o distorsionarlo. Esto resulta en confusión y falsa seguridad. La claridad en el evangelio es esencial para un testimonio fiel.

blocks.en: VII. Lack of Prayer
blocks.es_reference: VII. Falta de Oración

blocks.en: Evangelism without prayer becomes mere human effort. Paul emphasized prayer:
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo sin oración se convierte en mero esfuerzo humano. Pablo enfatizó la oración:

blocks.en: "Continue earnestly in prayer, being vigilant in it with thanksgiving." (Colossians 4:2, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Perseverad en la oración, velando en ella con acción de gracias." (Colosenses 4:2, RVG)

blocks.en: Prayer prepares the heart of the believer and the heart of the hearer.
blocks.es_reference: La oración prepara el corazón del creyente y el corazón del oyente.

blocks.en: VIII. The Influence of Culture
blocks.es_reference: VIII. La Influencia de la Cultura

blocks.en: Cultural pressure can discourage evangelism. In some settings, sharing the gospel may be viewed as offensive, intrusive, or inappropriate. However, the standard is not culture, but Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: La presión cultural puede desalentar el evangelismo. En algunos entornos, compartir el evangelio puede ser visto como ofensivo, intrusivo o inapropiado. Sin embargo, el estándar no es la cultura, sino la Escritura.

blocks.en: "We ought to obey God rather than men." (Acts 5:29, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Respondiendo Pedro y los apóstoles, dijeron: Es necesario obedecer a Dios antes que a los hombres." (Hechos 5:29, RVG)

blocks.en: IX. Illustration and Application
blocks.es_reference: IX. Ilustración y Aplicación

blocks.en: Consider two believers. One allows fear, distraction, and uncertainty to prevent him from speaking. Opportunities pass, and evangelism becomes rare. Another recognizes these obstacles, addresses them biblically, and moves forward in faith. He may still feel fear, but he does not allow it to control his actions. The difference is not the absence of obstacles, but the response to them.
blocks.es_reference: Considere a dos creyentes. Uno permite que el temor, la distracción y la incertidumbre le impidan hablar. Las oportunidades pasan, y el evangelismo se vuelve raro. Otro reconoce estos obstáculos, los aborda bíblicamente y avanza en fe. Puede seguir sintiendo temor, pero no permite que controle sus acciones. La diferencia no es la ausencia de obstáculos, sino la respuesta a ellos.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: Obstacles to evangelism are real, but they are not insurmountable. Fear, inadequacy, misplaced responsibility, lack of urgency, distraction, misunderstanding, and cultural pressure can all hinder witness. However, when these are addressed through Scripture, the believer is freed to act in faith. Evangelism is not dependent on perfect circumstances, but on faithful obedience.
blocks.es_reference: Los obstáculos para el evangelismo son reales, pero no son insuperables. El temor, la insuficiencia, la responsabilidad mal entendida, la falta de urgencia, la distracción, el malentendido y la presión cultural pueden todos estorbar el testimonio. Sin embargo, cuando estos se abordan a través de la Escritura, el creyente queda libre para actuar en fe. El evangelismo no depende de circunstancias perfectas, sino de la obediencia fiel.

sa.prompt: Explain why rejection is to be expected in evangelism, and distinguish between rejection of the message and rejection of the messenger (John 15:20).
sa.model: Rejection is to be expected in evangelism because John 15:20 says that if they persecuted Christ, they will persecute His servants. The believer must distinguish rejection of the message from rejection of the messenger: when people refuse the gospel, they are most often rejecting Christ and His claims, not the witness personally. Understanding this frees the believer from taking it as personal failure and keeps him faithful even when the response is hostile.

sa.prompt: Using the example of Moses (Exodus 4:10), explain the obstacle of fear of inadequacy and why the believer does not need to know everything.
sa.model: In Exodus 4:10 Moses pleaded that he was not eloquent, fearing his inadequacy. God's answer was that He made the mouth and would be with it. The obstacle of fear of inadequacy is the belief that one must know everything to witness. But the believer does not need to know everything; he needs only to point to Christ and trust God to supply what is lacking. God equips the willing and uses the inadequate who depend on Him.

sa.prompt: Describe the obstacle of misplaced responsibility. Using 1 Corinthians 3:6, explain whose work conviction and conversion are.
sa.model: The obstacle of misplaced responsibility is feeling that the believer must produce conversions himself. 1 Corinthians 3:6 corrects this: Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. Conviction and conversion are God's work, not the witness's. The believer is responsible to plant and water — to share faithfully — but the increase belongs to God alone. Seeing this lifts a burden no one was meant to carry and keeps him from despair when results do not come.

sa.prompt: Explain how a lack of urgency hinders evangelism, and how Matthew 25:46 restores a proper sense of urgency.
sa.model: A lack of urgency hinders evangelism by letting the believer treat the lost as if they have unlimited time, postponing witness indefinitely. Matthew 25:46 restores proper urgency by declaring that the lost go away into eternal punishment while the righteous enter eternal life. The eternal stakes mean today matters: people are perishing, judgment is real, and the opportunity to speak may not come again. This awakens the believer from complacency to seize the moment.

sa.prompt: Discuss how distractions and competing priorities (Mark 4:19) can choke the believer's witness, and how this obstacle is overcome.
sa.model: Mark 4:19 warns that the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, making it unfruitful. Distractions and competing priorities choke the believer's witness the same way: busyness, comfort, and lesser concerns crowd out evangelism until it never happens. This obstacle is overcome by deliberately keeping the lost and the gospel a priority — guarding time, refusing to let good things crowd out the essential, and intentionally making witness part of ordinary life.

sa.prompt: Explain why clarity in the gospel is essential, and what results when the gospel is omitted, oversimplified, or distorted.
sa.model: Clarity in the gospel is essential because a person cannot respond rightly to what he does not understand. When the gospel is omitted, the hearer gets morality or comfort but no way of salvation. When it is oversimplified, key truths like sin, the cross, or repentance are lost and the response is shallow. When it is distorted, a false gospel is believed that cannot save. In each case the result is confusion or false assurance rather than genuine faith, which is why the witness must keep the gospel clear and complete.

sa.prompt: Using Colossians 4:2, explain why evangelism without prayer becomes 'mere human effort,' and how prayer prepares both the believer and the hearer.
sa.model: Colossians 4:2 calls believers to continue steadfastly in prayer. Without prayer, evangelism becomes mere human effort because it relies on the witness's skill rather than God's power. Prayer prepares the believer by giving boldness, the right words, and dependence on the Spirit; and it prepares the hearer as God softens the heart and opens it before and during the conversation. Prayer connects the work to the only One who can grant the new birth, keeping evangelism God-dependent.

sa.prompt: Discuss the obstacle of cultural pressure. Using Acts 5:29, explain why Scripture, not culture, must be the believer's standard.
sa.model: The obstacle of cultural pressure is the fear of being thought intolerant or offensive, which tempts the believer to stay silent or soften the gospel. Acts 5:29 answers it: we must obey God rather than men. Scripture, not culture, must be the believer's standard because culture changes and often opposes the gospel, while God's word is fixed and authoritative. When culture and Scripture conflict, the faithful witness submits to God's word and speaks the truth despite the pressure.

sa.prompt: The unit contrasts two believers facing the same obstacles. Explain the difference between them and the lesson it teaches about responding to obstacles.
sa.model: The unit contrasts two believers facing the same obstacles — fear, rejection, distraction. The difference is not their circumstances but their response: one lets the obstacles silence him, while the other responds in faith, depending on God and obeying despite the difficulty. The lesson is that obstacles are common to all witnesses; what determines fruitfulness is whether the believer yields to them or overcomes them by faith, prayer, and dependence on the Spirit.

sa.prompt: Synthesize the unit: name several obstacles to evangelism and explain how each is answered biblically, concluding with what evangelism ultimately depends on.
sa.model: Evangelism faces several obstacles, each answered biblically. Fear of inadequacy is answered by God's promise to equip, as with Moses. Rejection is answered by remembering they rejected Christ first. Misplaced responsibility is answered because God gives the increase. Lack of urgency is answered by eternity's reality. Distraction is answered by keeping the gospel a priority. Cultural pressure is answered by obeying God over men. And prayerlessness is answered by steadfast prayer. In the end, overcoming every obstacle depends not on the believer's strength but on his dependence on God.
